catalog.detail.config: What goes into the AI tool’s configuration
catalog.detail.hint.agent: This is the agent as installed on your computer. Its memory and working directories stay on your computer and are not overwritten by updates.
catalog.detail.hint.mcp: No secret appears in the configuration: the command line injects your locally stored secret as an environment variable when it starts the MCP server.
catalog.detail.hint.on_demand: On demand: only a short skill goes into the skills directory, so the tool definitions do not sit in the AI’s context; the command line adds your secret when a tool is called.
catalog.detail.hint.skill: This is everything that lands on your computer and that the AI reads.
catalog.detail.hint.workflow: The slash command only tells the AI to fetch the steps; the command line hands out each step once the previous one has passed its checks.
catalog.detail.how.agent: In your AI tool, ask for it by name: “have {{name}} do it”
catalog.detail.mine.fresh: You have not connected a computer yet. Once you do, it is installed into your AI tools.
catalog.detail.mine.next_sync: Not there yet: it is installed at the next sync.
catalog.detail.mine.off: You have not turned it on, so it is not installed.
catalog.detail.mine.status: To see exactly which files it wrote:
catalog.detail.needs.local.hint: Each computer sets these for itself; the values are never uploaded. It installs without them, and the AI asks when it needs one.
catalog.detail.steps.hint: A “command” check runs on your computer and passes only with exit code 0; a “person” check needs your reply in the AI tool; an “AI self-check” must show evidence. Tools without slash commands get this workflow as a skill.
